_readme: Stat weights for LEVELLING on World of Warcraft: Forever. A first pass,
meant to be argued with and tuned, not treated as settled.
The thing that makes these different from raid weights is the cost
function. At 60 in a raid you are maximising damage over a fight you
will repeat. While levelling you are minimising time to the next level,
and the biggest drain on that is downtime: drinking, dying, running
back. So Stamina and Spirit carry far more weight here than any endgame
list would give them, and that is deliberate rather than sloppy.
Weights are per point, scaled so the class's primary stat is 1.0. They
are linear on purpose. At these levels there are no meaningful caps or
proc interactions to model, which is exactly why a weighted score is
honest here and a simulation would be false precision.
Weapons are NOT scored against armour. Their damage per second swamps
any stat line, so mixing them into one ranking produces a list that
says 'your best helm is a sword'. They are ranked separately.

WARRIOR._note: Arms or Fury while levelling. Strength is damage, Stamina is uptime.

WARRIOR_PROT._note: Only if you are actually tanking instances. Staying alive outranks damage.

PALADIN._note: Retribution. Some Intellect earns its place because heals and seals cost mana.

HUNTER._note: Agility is damage, crit and armour at once. Intellect only to keep stings up.

ROGUE._note: No mana, no downtime beyond eating, so Stamina matters less than for most.

PRIEST._note: Shadow or Discipline. Spirit is the levelling stat: it decides how often you sit.

SHAMAN._note: Enhancement. Agility and Strength both pull, and mana still matters.

MAGE._note: Cloth and no escape beyond Blink, so Stamina is not the throwaway it is at 60.

WARLOCK._note: Stamina is higher than the other casters: it feeds Life Tap and the pet tanks.

DRUID._note: Feral. Agility leads, Strength close behind, and you still want some mana to shift.

_note: Weapons are ranked by damage per second first, with stats as a
tiebreak. The exchange rate below says how many points of the
primary stat one point of DPS is worth, which is a rough figure and
the first thing to revisit once anything can be measured in game.
Casters are the exception: their weapon is a stat stick, so DPS
hardly matters and the stats do.
